newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso crashes 15.65 pesos vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso crashes 15.65 pesos vs dollar.

text.p: Colombia's peso crashed 15.65 pesos against the dollar Monday to close at 1,051.20, its lowest level since Aug. 15, interbank traders said.

The peso was pushed down by companies buying dollars to service foreign debts in advance of further anticipated drops in the value of the peso, and banks buying greenbacks after selling heavily Friday, traders said.
Interbank traders added that as interest rates fell, traditional fixed income investors were looking elsewhere for profits.

Coupled with the rising demand for greenbacks, fewer dollars than normal were coming into the markets following government emergency measures to stem the tide of newly contracted foreign debt in both the public and the private sector, traders said.

Dealers reported 494 operations worth a total $224 million, above the daily average of about $180 million. The peso hit an intraday high of 1,036.5 and sank to an intraday low of 1,052.55 pesos per dollar.

The fall put the peso at its lowest level since Aug. 15. The peso closed 1996 at 1,009.45 against the dollar after a year in which it dropped just 1.79 percent in nominal terms, compared with a forecast devaluation of 13.5 percent.
The central bank and the government have fixed a minimum target of 15 percent devaluation of the peso for 1997. In the year to date the interbank value of the peso has already fallen 4.1 percent.
